dedupe_keys.name: infoantenas radio stations and exposure levels map spain

description: Infoantenas is the Spanish ministry's public service on radio stations and radio-frequency exposure levels, and in practice the only official source for the location of mobile telephone antennas in Spain. Through a map viewer in the ministry's geoportal it shows each mobile base station with its operator, assigned frequency bands and technology from 2G to 5G, together with exposure measurements taken around stations. The data come from inspections by the provincial telecommunications inspection offices and from certificates that mobile operators must submit to the ministry, and the ministry publishes annual reports on exposure levels, such as the 2024 report. Although built to let citizens check exposure, the viewer is widely used, including by third-party apps listed on the national open data portal, to find stations and judge coverage. Coverage: Spain, all licensed mobile stations, kept up to date. Format and access: web map viewer and annual PDF reports, free; the service is catalogued in the Spanish spatial data infrastructure, but a bulk download or API was not found and users on datos.gob.es have asked for one. Caveats: positions and details are as certified by operators; exposure measurements are periodic samples. Simulation uses: asset inventory of mobile networks for hazard exposure and coverage studies, and cross-checking crowdsourced cell locations. Related records: the CNMC geographic statistics give counts by province, OpenCelliD gives crowdsourced locations, and ANFR's Cartoradio plays the same role in France.
